cue: How do you say someone panics over nothing?

es.text: Ahogarse en un vaso de agua
es.literal: to drown oneself in a glass of water
es.meaning: To be overwhelmed by a trivial problem.
es.example: Es un correo, no te ahogues en un vaso de agua.
es.exampleTranslation: It's one email — don't make a crisis out of nothing.

it.literal: to drown in a glass of water
it.meaning: To be overwhelmed by a trivial problem.
it.example: È una mail, non affogare in un bicchier d'acqua.
it.exampleTranslation: It's one email — don't make a crisis out of nothing.

bridge.note: Identical picture, three small things wrong with the crossing. The glass is a false friend — Spanish vaso, Italian bicchiere, because an Italian vaso holds flowers. Spanish drowns you reflexively, ahogarSE, doing it to yourself; Italian just drowns, affogare, no pronoun. And Italian clips the noun inside the phrase: bicchier d'acqua, not bicchiere d'acqua, an apocopation that only happens because the word is leaning on what follows it.

interference.es_to_it: Three at once. No reflexive — 'affogarsi in un bicchier d'acqua' is wrong, Italian says affogare. The glass is a bicchiere, never a vaso. And keep the clipped form, bicchier d'acqua; the full bicchiere sounds heavy inside the idiom even though it is the correct word on its own.
interference.it_to_es: Spanish needs the reflexive back — ahogarSE — and the glass is a vaso. Spanish does not clip: it is un vaso de agua, in full. SEE ALSO 0265 and 0266, where the same vaso/bicchiere false friend appears in the half-full/half-empty pair.
